name: Productized data cleaning, PDF-to-Excel conversion and data-entry gigs
summary: Fixed-price gigs that clean, dedupe, reformat or extract data from client files, done mostly by scripts and LLMs with a human check.
howItWorks: List fixed-scope gigs: PDF/scan to Excel, CSV cleanup, CRM dedupe, sheet merges. Small businesses pay because the work is tedious. A pipeline (OCR, pandas, LLM extraction) does most of each order; you spot-check and deliver. Repeat buyers send monthly batches.

payout.notes: Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer fee (2025 change). Not re-confirmed Nov 2026: Fiverr/Upwork help pages block automated checks.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Personal data in files triggers GDPR-type duties.

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer; PayPal receiving missing in some (e.g. Bangladesh).

automationPlan: OCR + LLM extraction scripts per gig type
validation rules and diff reports before delivery
templated order replies and delivery messages
evidence: Data entry/conversion are large Fiverr/Upwork categories; Fiverr permits AI in all categories if output is refined per client.

skills: basic Python or Power Query (AI coding assistants cover most of it)
accounts: Fiverr seller account + ID verification
Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate from typical Fiverr data-entry/PDF-to-Excel package tiers ($10 basic to $100-$200 bulk); fee = Fiverr 20%; cost = AI/OCR credits. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026. ChatGPT Plus (~$20/mo) and Canva Pro (~$15/mo) prices are estimated: their pricing pages were bot-blocked.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order.

marketConditions.notes: Thousands of low-cost sellers (many in South Asia) compete at $5-$15, and since 2024-2025 many buyers do simple conversions themselves with ChatGPT or Excel Copilot. Winners specialize (messy scanned invoices, CRM migrations, recurring monthly batches) and win repeat B2B buyers. The median starter nets under $100/month by month 12; failure modes are zero visibility for new gigs and underpricing.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a $10-$20 basic tier capped by row/page count to collect the first 10 reviews, then reprice per 1,000 rows/pages and push monthly batch packages at $100+.
profitPath: Month 0: build an OCR + pandas + LLM extraction pipeline and 3 gigs with sample before/after files (cost $0-$20)
Month 1-2: first 5-15 small orders at $10-$30, expected $50-$200 gross
Month 3-6: raise prices after reviews, add bulk/recurring tiers, bid on Upwork batch jobs
Month 6-12: convert repeat buyers to monthly retainers; target 10-20 orders/month

name: Logo/brand kits and image editing (background removal, upscaling) gigs

howItWorks: Packages: logo + palette + fonts + social templates, or bulk product-photo background removal, upscaling and resizing. AI generates concepts and batch edits; you vectorize, refine and check. Buyers are new businesses and online sellers wanting fast, consistent assets.

payout.notes: Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer fee (2025 change). Not re-confirmed Nov 2026: Fiverr/Upwork help pages block automated checks.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Purely AI-generated images may not be copyrightable (e.g. US), so disclose and add human vector work for logos.
complianceRequirements: use tools whose licenses allow commercial output

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer; PayPal receiving missing in some (e.g. Bangladesh).

manualSteps: vector cleanup and final design choices
evidence: Fiverr runs dedicated logo and image-editing categories with high order volume; its AI guidelines allow AI if seller holds rights to delivered content.

tools: Canva Pro or Figma free tier (~$15/mo for Canva)

name: Transcription and subtitle (SRT/VTT) service with ASR + human QA
summary: Sell accurate transcripts and burned-in or sidecar subtitles; Whisper-class ASR does the draft, you proofread.
howItWorks: YouTubers, podcasters and course creators pay for accurate transcripts and timed captions. ASR gives a 90-95% draft; you fix names, jargon and timing, then deliver SRT/VTT/DOCX. Translated subtitles are an upsell.

payout.notes: Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer fee (2025 change). Not re-confirmed Nov 2026: Fiverr/Upwork help pages block automated checks.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Legal/medical transcription can have confidentiality rules (e.g. HIPAA in the US); avoid unless compliant.

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer; PayPal receiving missing in some (e.g. Bangladesh).

automationPlan: auto subtitle segmentation and line-length rules
risks: clients can run free ASR themselves, pushing prices down
evidence: Transcription and subtitling remain active Fiverr/Upwork categories; Fiverr permits AI-assisted delivery when refined to client needs.

skills: excellent written grammar in the target language
accounts: Fiverr seller account + ID verification
Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

Month 3-6: add translation subtitles and research-interview transcription; pitch podcasters directly

name: Machine-translation post-editing (MTPE) and localization
summary: Post-edit machine/LLM translations into your native language for websites, apps, e-commerce listings and documents.
howItWorks: Businesses localizing content pay for fluent human review of machine output. You run MT/LLM, then edit for accuracy, tone and terminology. Work comes via Smartcat marketplace, Upwork, Fiverr and agencies. Native speakers of mid-demand languages have an edge.

payout.minimumPayout: Smartcat: self-set auto-payout threshold (each method has its own minimum); Fiverr $1-$20
payout.frequency: Smartcat automatic once balance hits threshold; Fiverr on demand
payout.notes: Smartcat takes no commission from freelancers; withdrawal fee 0.5% + fixed $1-$10 by method (since 27 Mar 2026), FX ~2.5% over mid-market; funds arrive within 5 business days. Fiverr 14-day clearance.

legality.notes: Ordinary translation is legal everywhere. Certified/sworn/court translation requires a license in many countries; exclude it.
complianceRequirements: disclose MT use when client requires

availability.notes: Smartcat, Upwork and Fiverr pay out globally via Payoneer/PayPal/bank; demand depends on language pair.

automationPlan: QA checks (numbers, tags, terms) by script
evidence: Smartcat's marketplace advertises 500K+ linguists, lets buyers add a human post-editing review to AI output, and lets freelancers set their own per-word rates; MTPE is a standard industry service.

skills: native-level target language and strong source language
accounts: Smartcat freelancer profile
Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
Fiverr seller account + ID verification
ProZ.com free profile
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: MTPE commonly pays ~40-60% of full translation rates ($0.02-$0.08/word); fee blends Smartcat 0% commission + withdrawal/FX costs with occasional Upwork/Fiverr work. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order. No fixed costs.

marketConditions.notes: LLM translation quality jumped in 2024-2026 and agencies have shifted volume from full translation to cheaper post-editing, pushing per-word rates down. Native speakers of less-served languages (Nordic, Baltic, Southeast Asian, African languages) and those with legal/medical/technical specialization still get steady work. Failure modes: commodity language pairs (EN-ES, EN-FR) at bottom rates, and slow agency vetting.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Quote per word with a minimum fee per job; take agency test jobs at standard MTPE rates, then raise rates for specialized domains and rush delivery.
profitPath: Month 0: complete Smartcat/ProZ profiles, pass agency tests, build termbases (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first small jobs, expected $50-$200
Month 3-6: win 1-2 recurring agency or e-commerce clients
Month 6-12: specialize in one domain; target 30-60k words/month

name: AI automation agency (Zapier / Make / n8n builds for SMBs)

howItWorks: SMBs pay to remove manual work: lead routing, invoicing, CRM sync, AI email triage. You scope, build in Make/Zapier/n8n, document and hand over or maintain on retainer. Clients come from Upwork, Contra, the Make and Zapier Solution Partner directories and local networking. Affiliate programs (Make 35% for 12 months, n8n 30% for 12 months) add referral income.

Podcast editing holds up better because it needs judgment. Voice Library royalties pay most voices only a few dollars a month. Failure modes: commodity TTS pricing and voice-rights disputes.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Undercut on turnaround (same day) for the first reviews, then sell bundled podcast packages (edit + show notes + clips) at monthly rates.
profitPath: Month 0: subscribe to a commercial-license voice plan, produce demo reels (cost $22)
Month 1-2: first orders at $10-$30, expected $50-$150
Month 3-6: podcast editing clients on monthly packages
Month 6-12: 3-8 recurring podcasts plus voiceover orders

name: Remote virtual assistant and bookkeeping (BELAY, Fancy Hands, Upwork, OnlineJobs.ph)
summary: Paid VA and bookkeeping work through staffing networks or Upwork, using AI to handle inbox, scheduling, data entry and reconciliation faster.
howItWorks: Busy executives and small businesses pay for admin and bookkeeping hours. US residents (outside six states) can apply to BELAY's 1099 contractor roles; Fancy Hands pays $3-$7 per task to start; others find VA/bookkeeping clients on Upwork or OnlineJobs.ph (Philippines-focused job board). AI drafts emails, categorizes transactions and summarizes documents, letting you serve more clients per hour.

methods: OnlineJobs.ph: employer pays worker directly (e.g. EasyPay)
payout.minimumPayout: none stated for BELAY/Fancy Hands; Upwork varies
payout.notes: BELAY lists no pay rates officially ($18-$23/h is from third-party reviews); hours vary with client needs. Fancy Hands pays biweekly. OnlineJobs.ph employers pay weekly in arrears.

legality.notes: VA and bookkeeping are legal; tax filing/advice and statutory accounting need licenses in many countries (e.g. Germany StBerG), so limit to bookkeeping/data entry.

availability.notes: BELAY accepts US residents except CA, CO, MT, NJ, NY, PA. Fancy Hands' application page states no residency rule (historically US-focused). OnlineJobs.ph targets Filipino workers. Upwork covers most reference countries.

fullCycle: Apply to network or build Upwork profile
risks: low per-task pay at Fancy Hands
evidence: BELAY's careers page lists remote 1099 bookkeeping and executive-assistant contractor roles; Fancy Hands' application page states $3-$7 per task paid every other Tuesday. Score 6 reflects accessible per-task/Upwork entry, though BELAY wants prior professional experience.

accounts: Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
OnlineJobs.ph profile (Philippines-focused)
BELAY/Fancy Hands application (US only)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: OnlineJobs.ph VA roles ~$3-$7/h, Upwork general VAs $8-$20/h, bookkeeping $20-$35/h, BELAY $18-$23/h (third-party); fee ~10% Upwork blended with 0% direct. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order. No fixed costs; profit equals hours billed.

marketConditions.notes: VA work is steady because clients buy reliability and time zone coverage, not output volume; AI raises a VA's throughput but also lets clients do simple tasks themselves. Competition from the Philippines, Latin America and Africa keeps general VA rates low; bookkeeping pays more. Failure mode: income stops when hours stop; it is labor, not automation.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Accept a modest hourly rate for the first long-term client, then move to monthly packages (e.g. 20 h/month) and raise rates with bookkeeping or industry specialization.
profitPath: Month 0: profiles, free QuickBooks/Xero certification, sample SOPs (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first part-time client, expected $100-$400
Month 3-6: 10-20 h/week across 1-3 clients
Month 6-12: shift to bookkeeping/executive support rates

name: Technical writing and API documentation
summary: Write API references, developer guides and tutorials for software companies, with AI generating first drafts from code and specs.
howItWorks: Dev-tool companies pay $150-$1,500 per article or doc set. You read the code/OpenAPI spec, use an LLM to draft reference docs and examples, then test every snippet and edit. Work comes from Upwork, Contra and developer-content agencies such as Draft.dev that pay developer-writers per article.
platforms: Draft.dev and similar developer content agencies

payout.notes: Upwork variable 0-15% fee (not re-confirmed; page blocks automated checks); Contra 0% freelancer commission. Draft.dev confirms it pays writers but publishes no rates.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere. Many publishers require human-authored work or AI disclosure; follow each client's policy.

availability.notes: Upwork 180+ countries; Contra pays out via local bank, PayPal, Payoneer or crypto.

automationPlan: auto-run and test code samples in CI
evidence: Technical writing is a well-paid Upwork category; Upwork ToS allows AI use if work is not misrepresented.

skills: running and testing every code sample
accounts: Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
Contra profile
applications to developer-content agencies (e.g. Draft.dev)
Wise Business or Stripe account for invoicing (KYC)

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate from Upwork technical-writing contracts and agency rates ($150-$1,500 per article); fee ~10% Upwork blended with 0% Contra/direct. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order.

marketConditions.notes: Dev-tool companies still pay for accurate, tested docs and tutorials, but AI drafts have cut the hours per piece and some companies now generate reference docs automatically. Writers who can actually run the code win; non-developers struggle to pass agency tests. Content-marketing budgets at startups are cyclical.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Build 3 public sample tutorials, take the first agency articles at standard rates, then sell doc-set projects priced per endpoint or per page.

Month 1-3: first 1-2 paid articles, expected $200-$600
Month 3-6: recurring agency slot or 1 direct client

name: Code review, bug fixing and dev help via Codementor, Topcoder and Toptal
summary: Earn from on-demand debugging/mentoring (Codementor), competitive challenges (Topcoder) and vetted contracts (Toptal), with coding agents speeding delivery.
howItWorks: Developers pay for live help and fixes on Codementor; companies post paid challenges on Topcoder (winners paid); Toptal places vetted freelancers in contracts. Coding agents help you reproduce bugs, write fixes and tests quickly, but you stay accountable and must follow each platform's rules on live sessions and original submissions.

methods: Topcoder: bank transfer via Trolley (only option since 21 Oct 2025)
payout.minimumPayout: Topcoder: none published; Codementor $1 min fee per transfer
payout.frequency: on demand / per challenge / per invoice
payout.notes: Topcoder/Trolley fee $1, $2 or $9 by country (+2% FX), 3-5 business days; needs W-8BEN/W-9 + ID. Codementor withdrawal fees: PayPal $1 (US) or 2% ($1-$20), Stripe 0.3% (min $1), local bank ~$3-$7. Codementor platform fee (~13-22%) not re-confirmed.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; respect client IP and licenses of AI-generated code.

availability.notes: Topcoder pays by bank transfer via Trolley (broad but not universal country coverage); Codementor via PayPal/Stripe/local bank; Toptal accepts fewer than 3% of applicants.

automationPlan: challenge spec parsing and submission checklists
evidence: Topcoder documents its Trolley bank payouts and fees; Codementor documents withdrawal fees; Toptal states it accepts fewer than 3% of 200,000+ yearly applicants.

skills: professional-level programming in at least one stack
accounts: Codementor mentor profile
Topcoder member + Trolley payout (W-8BEN/W-9 + ID)
Toptal application (screening <3% acceptance)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: Codementor sessions $20-$100/h, Toptal contracts $50-$120/h; fee ~15% is an estimate of Codementor's commission, which its help page does not publish (it lists only withdrawal fees: PayPal 2%, Stripe 0.3%); Topcoder prizes vary.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order.

marketConditions.notes: Coding assistants now answer most junior debugging questions, cutting on-demand mentoring demand, while Toptal-style vetted contracts still pay well but are hard to enter. Topcoder challenges are competitive with uncertain wins. Experienced specialists (niche stacks, performance, security) earn; beginners rarely do.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start slightly below market to get first ratings on Codementor, then raise to your niche's rate and move clients to longer contracts.
profitPath: Month 0: profiles, portfolio repos, payout KYC (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first sessions/challenges, expected $0-$300
Month 3-6: repeat mentees or one longer contract
Month 6-12: part-time contract work for those who pass vetting

name: Paid expert consultations (GLG, AlphaSights, Guidepoint) and paid Q&A (JustAnswer)
summary: Get paid per call or per answer for professional knowledge; AI helps prepare briefings and research, the answers are yours.
howItWorks: Investors and consultants pay expert networks for 30-60 minute calls with industry practitioners; you set an hourly rate (often $100-$500). JustAnswer pays verified professionals a share of customer payments per answer. AI speeds research, but advice must be your own; licensed fields need a license.

payout.notes: Guidepoint pays typically within 15 days of a completed consultation (invoice within 45 days; prorated by full minutes). GLG pays an hourly rate or pre-disclosed flat fee, optionally to your employer. AlphaSights timing and JustAnswer revenue share/schedule not confirmed (sites block automated checks).

legality.notes: Legal; never share employer confidential info or material non-public information (securities law). Legal/medical/financial answers require a valid license.

availability.notes: Expert networks recruit globally but demand favors industry experience; JustAnswer accepts experts in many countries after verification.

automationPlan: AI briefing notes per call topic
fullCycle: Create profiles with detailed work history
evidence: GLG states members are paid a set hourly rate or flat fee; Guidepoint's advisor terms pay your customary consulting fee, typically within 15 days. Reports cite typical $175/h GLG calls.

tools: LLM free tier for call prep
skills: 5+ years of real industry or professional expertise
accounts: GLG/AlphaSights/Guidepoint expert profiles
JustAnswer expert application with credential verification
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Expert networks pay the expert's own rate; reports cite ~$175/h typical GLG calls; network margin is charged to the client, so fee = 0 to the expert. JustAnswer pays a revenue share per answer; the share is estimated, as its expert page was bot-blocked.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order. No costs; income is sporadic.

marketConditions.notes: Calls depend entirely on whether a client project needs your exact niche; many registered experts get no calls in a year. AI research tools and transcript libraries (e.g. expert-call transcript databases) have reduced repeat calls on common topics. Those with current, rare operating roles in hot sectors get regular requests.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Set a rate near your salary-equivalent hourly x2-3; raise it after repeat requests and decline low-fit calls.
profitPath: Month 0: register with 3 networks and complete detailed profiles (cost $0)
Month 1-6: respond quickly to project invitations; expected 0-2 calls
Month 6-12: repeat clients in your niche; JustAnswer answers if credentialed
